To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

rare-earth alloying elements in low-temperature solding alloys can produce direct bonding of a variety of electronic components and optical fiber in air, without flux, at low temperatures, and with very high bond strengths.

(1) a new type of lead-free solders containing RE alloying elements, such as Lu, can be used to produce strong, direct bonds on the surfaces of various inorganic materials, including nitrides, carbide, oxides, diamond, and Si, (2) the bonding is achieved without using flux, (3) the bonding is based upon chemical reactions between the solder and the inorganic surface, and hence, the bonding can be very strong and reliable, and (4)

the addition of rare earth alloying elements to the Sn-Ag, Sn-Cu, and Sn-Ag-Cu solders improves their wettability and bonding ability to a variety of in-organic materials, such that the bond strength is enhanced by a factor of up to 5.5 times that of the conventional lead-based solders.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of lead-free universal solders containing REs, such as La, Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm, Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho, Er, Tm, and Yb, for use in electronic and optical assemblies.
the development of lead-free, low-melting-temperature solders for electronic assemblies.
developing new lead-free solders for optical, electronic, and other devices, which are based on the use of rare earth alloying elements.

the use of REs as alloying additions in low-melting-temperature solders can provide a new approach to soldering and bonding of difficult-to-bond surfaces.

the addition of a few percent of a low-meltingpoint RE element to a low-mel-ting-point solder, such as Sn-Ag, Sn-Zn, or Sn-Cu, can result in a strong, low-temperature solder alloy that can be used to bond a wide variety of electronic and optical materials.
the addition of RE elements into the low-melting-temperature solders can be used to obtain direct bonding of a wide range of materials in the absence of flux.

the use of low-melting-temperature solders with rare-earth alloying elements is a very effective approach for producing strong bonds on the surfaces of a variety of difficult-to-bond inorganic materials.
the RE elements can be used as alloying elements in the low-temperature soldering process for bonding a variety of electronic and optical components.
we have developed a new approach for the direct bonding of difficult-to-solder surfaces.

the use of RE elements in solder alloys is a promising approach for producing low-cost and reliable bonding on a variety of surfaces.
